method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. claims.claim: **Prophylaxis treats at-risk contacts to eliminate nasopharyngeal carriage**, cutting transmission and secondary cases. **Give it as soon as possible.**
claims.source_text: Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal and Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) disease involves the treatment of at-risk contacts to eliminate nasopharyngeal carriage, thereby reducing transmission and the risk of secondary cases; it should be given to contacts as soon as possible
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give prophylaxis early to both the index case and contacts**, especially for *N. meningitidis*, because secondary cases can develop rapidly.
claims.source_text: Prophylaxis must be given early to both the index case and contacts, especially for N. meningitidis disease, because of the rapidity with which secondary cases may develop
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Local susceptibility patterns may change the choice** — check local guidelines.
claims.source_text: Antimicrobial recommendations may vary according to local antimicrobial susceptibility patterns. Refer to local guidelines
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **_N. meningitidis_ contacts needing prophylaxis:** close, prolonged contact from 7 days before symptom onset until 24 hours after the case's antibiotics began — household (highest risk); same childcare group (two full 6–8 hour days, or 20 hours cumulative); intimate (kissing); healthcare workers with unprotected close airway exposure and inadequate PPE; passengers seated immediately next to the case for more than 8 hours.
claims.source_text: Neisseria meningitidis Requires contact prophylaxis Close and prolonged contact within 7 days prior to the onset of symptoms until 24 hours after antibiotic treatment including Household contacts (highest risk group) Childcare contact in same care group (equivalent degree of contact as a household contact) Two full 6-8 hour days Or Cumulative 20 hours of contact Intimate contacts (kissing) Healthcare workers who have unprotected close airway exposure and inadequate PPE Passengers sitting immediately adjacent to a case for >8 hours
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk of meningococcal disease is highest 7–10 days after exposure**; effective clearance antibiotics eliminate meningococci from the nasopharynx within 24 hours.
claims.source_text: The risk of developing meningococcal disease is highest in the 7-10 days after exposure … Meningococci are eliminated from the nasopharynx within 24 hours of commencing effective clearance antibiotic therapy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ciprofloxacin, oral, single dose:** under 5 years 30 mg/kg (max 125 mg); 5–12 years 250 mg; 12 years and over 500 mg.
claims.source_text: Ciprofloxacin PO as a single dose <5 years: 30 mg/kg (max 125 mg) 5-12 years: 250 mg ≥12 years: 500 mg
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rifampicin, oral, twice daily for 2 days:** under 1 month 5 mg/kg; 1 month and over 10 mg/kg (max 600 mg).
claims.source_text: Rifampicin PO BD for 2 days <1 month: 5 mg/kg (<1 month) ≥1 month: 10 mg/kg (max 600 mg)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rifampicin is preferred in neonates; ceftriaxone is preferred in pregnancy.** ⚠️ **Rifampicin is contraindicated in pregnancy and severe liver disease.**
claims.source_text: Ceftriaxone is preferred in pregnancy. Rifampicin is preferred in neonates … Rifampicin is contraindicated in pregnancy and severe liver disease
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pregnancy or rifampicin contraindicated: ceftriaxone IM, single dose** — 12 years and over 250 mg; 1 month to 12 years 125 mg.
claims.source_text: Pregnancy or contraindication to Rifampicin: Ceftriaxone IM as a single dose ≥12 years: 250 mg 1 month to 12 years: 125 mg
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer vaccination to non-immunised contacts** of serogroup A, C, W or Y cases.
claims.source_text: Vaccination should be offered to non-immunised contacts of cases with N. meningitidis serogroups A, C, W or Y
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The Hib index patient needs prophylaxis unless treated with ceftriaxone/cefotaxime.**
claims.source_text: Haemophilus influenzae type b Requires contact prophylaxis The index patient if they have not been treated with ceftriaxone/cefotaxime
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hib contacts needing prophylaxis:** close, prolonged contact from 7 days before symptom onset until 48 hours after antibiotics — household contacts **only if the household contains a vulnerable contact**; childcare contacts with household-level contact who are themselves vulnerable; vulnerable contacts who shared a hospital room with the case; healthcare workers with unprotected close airway exposure and inadequate PPE.
claims.source_text: Close and prolonged contact within 7 days prior to the onset of symptoms until 48 hours after antibiotic treatment including Household contacts if the household contains a vulnerable contact (defined below) Childcare contacts if they have levels of contact of a household contact, and is a vulnerable contact Vulnerable contacts who have shared a hospital room with the index patient Healthcare workers who have unprotected close airway exposure and inadequate PPE
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vulnerable contact** = infant under 7 months (whatever the vaccination status) · immunocompromised or asplenic person of any age (whatever the vaccination status) · inadequately vaccinated child aged 7 months–2 years (childcare) or 7 months–5 years (household and hospital).
claims.source_text: The definition of a vulnerable contact is an infant <7 months of age (regardless of vaccination status) an immunocompromised or asplenic person of any age (regardless of vaccination status) Inadequately vaccinated per the following age and contact type Childcare: 7 months - 2 years Household and hospital: 7 months - 5 years
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rifampicin, oral, daily for 4 days:** under 1 month 10 mg/kg; 1 month and over 20 mg/kg (max 600 mg).
claims.source_text: Rifampicin PO daily for 4 days <1 month: 10 mg/kg ≥1 month: 20 mg/kg (max 600 mg)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pregnancy or rifampicin contraindicated: ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg (max 1 g) IM daily for 2 days.**
claims.source_text: Pregnancy or contraindication to Rifampicin Ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg (max 1 g) IM daily for 2 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Immunise children who are not up to date with Hib.**
claims.source_text: Children who are not up to date with Hib should be immunised
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **_Streptococcus pneumoniae_: no increased risk to contacts — no prophylaxis.**
claims.source_text: Streptococcus pneumoniae No increased risk to contacts Antibiotic prophylaxis not required
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Rifampicin induces the metabolism of many drugs** — including the oral contraceptive pill (use alternative contraception), anticonvulsants, warfarin and chloramphenicol. **Do a drug interaction check.**
claims.source_text: Induces the metabolism of multiple medications Including the oral contraceptive pill (alternative contraception should be instituted), anticonvulsants, warfarin and chloramphenicol A drug interaction check should be completed
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use rifampicin with hepatic impairment.** It is preferred in infants, though ciprofloxacin is safe and effective.
claims.source_text: Rifampicin should not be used if there is hepatic impairment Preferred in infants, although ciprofloxacin is safe and effective
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Contact prophylaxis for invasive meningococcal or Hib disease' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Contact_prophylaxis_for_invasive_meningococcal_or_Hib_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Warn that rifampicin turns body fluids red** — urine, saliva, tears (can damage soft contact lenses), sweat.
claims.source_text: Colours body fluids red, for example urine, saliva, tears (soft contact lenses may be damaged), sweat
